hypothesis: The r745 lobby error 174 ak47_mp is thrown by a native weapon-registration check after the signed fastfile becomes visible; capture the exact Com Error caller and predicate without changing the server payload.

r746.difference_from_r745: Same existing runtime, same signed ak47_mp.ff staged temporarily, same gamestate/snapshot and session flags; a temporary hook was added at the error function for attribution.
r746.replication: r745 and r746 independently showed the same 174 ak47_mp dialog with the signed file staged; n=2, no claim of stable success.

native_error_event.native_static: 0x58FCEB calls 0x4F82E0 with code 2, format 174 %s and the weapon definition's name only when [0x1C166E8 + weapon_id*16 + 4] == 0 (comparison at 0x58FCD4). This identifies the precise observed error predicate, not the cause of the zero slot.
native_error_event.upstream_registration_path: 0x58F370 can call 0x58EF60 at 0x58F723, passing the per-weapon 16-byte slot; 0x58EF60 writes slot+4 from 0x58ED10 at 0x58EFF2. Whether this call executes and what later clears the slot remain unmeasured.

failed_hook_attribution.observation: The launcher had already placed an INT3 breakpoint at 0x4F82E0; the direct hook would replay CC inside its cave. It was immediately restored. A hook at 0x4F82E1 recorded zero hits despite the dialog, because the launcher's breakpoint handler observes the event before the function body runs.
failed_hook_attribution.reuse: Read the launcher's existing events.jsonl breakpoint record; do not hook over its breakpoint for this error.

conclusion: The displayed 174 ak47_mp is directly tied to a zero per-weapon registration slot at 0x58FCD4 in this run. The reason that slot is zero is still open. Neither signed fastfile staging nor the temporary hooks produced a playable first-person weapon or shooting.
